pamphlet_excerpts: Causes of Diver Hyperventilation: Hyperventilation is the result of over breathing, either deliberately or because of panic (p. 21).
Dizziness and Suffocation Feelings: The likely result of hyperventilation is dizziness and fainting, and victims will feel as if they are being suffocated (p. 21).
Preparation Prevents Diving Panic: Such a condition is unlikely in diving if the participants are properly prepared for each new skill level (p. 21).
Calming a Panicked Diver: If a diver shows signs of panic at any time, bring that person back into the boat or onto shore, calm the person, and encourage slow breathing (p. 21).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Prepare Divers Before Entry: Such a condition is unlikely in diving if the participants are properly prepared for each new skill level (p. 21).
Step 2 - Bring Panicked Diver Ashore: If a diver shows signs of panic at any time, bring that person back into the boat or onto shore, calm the person, and encourage slow breathing (p. 21).
Step 3 - Provide Rest and Air: Make sure the person rests in a comfortable position and has plenty of open, fresh air (p. 21).
Step 4 - Resolve Underlying Panic Cause: Before resuming any activity, find out and resolve the cause of the panic (p. 21).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why is the most important rule in scuba diving to breathe continuously and never hold your breath while ascending with compressed air?
quiz_item.question: Why is the most important rule in scuba diving to breathe continuously and never hold your breath while ascending with compressed air?
options: A. Holding your breath causes nitrogen gas to freeze inside the first-stage regulator valve.
B. As water pressure decreases during ascent, trapped air in the lungs expands according to Boyle's Law and can rupture lung tissue (pulmonary barotrauma) if not exhaled.
C. Exhaling underwater fogs the inside of your dive mask and drains the buoyancy compensator vest.
D. Breathing continuously allows you to ascend faster than 60 feet per minute without making a safety stop.
choices: A. Holding your breath causes nitrogen gas to freeze inside the first-stage regulator valve.
B. As water pressure decreases during ascent, trapped air in the lungs expands according to Boyle's Law and can rupture lung tissue (pulmonary barotrauma) if not exhaled.
C. Exhaling underwater fogs the inside of your dive mask and drains the buoyancy compensator vest.
D. Breathing continuously allows you to ascend faster than 60 feet per minute without making a safety stop.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. As water pressure decreases during ascent, trapped air in the lungs expands according to Boyle's Law and can rupture lung tissue (pulmonary barotrauma) if not exhaled.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Under Boyle's Law, gas volume increases as surrounding water pressure drops during ascent; holding your breath while breathing compressed air traps expanding gas in the lungs, risking life-threatening pulmonary barotrauma.

Following Currents in Drift Dives: During adrift dive, divers follow a current and may finish the dive aconsiderable distance from where they started (p. 9).

Step 3 - Coordinate Dive Boat Pickup: Either a single dive boat, or small tenders from a live-aboard vessel, may follow the group and be ready to quickly pick up divers who may end the dive (p. 9).

pamphlet_excerpts: Medical Fitness for Diving: You may have one or more medical issues that may prevent you from scuba diving (p. 19).
Importance of Ascending Slowly: Adjusting to the Underwater World Decompression, The Importance of Going Up Slow As you dive, your time underwater has limits (p. 19).
Depth and Air Limits: These limits are affected by depth, your air supply, the cold, and fatigue (p. 19).
Increasing Underwater Body Pressure: The pressure on a diver's body increases with depth (p. 19).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Monitor Depth and Air: These limits are affected by depth, your air supply, the cold, and fatigue (p. 19).
Step 2 - Account for Increasing Pressure: The pressure on a diver's body increases with depth (p. 19).
Step 3 - Track Tissue Nitrogen Absorption: This increase in pressure causes nitrogen (the gas that makes up 79 percent of the air we breathe) to be absorbed into the body's tissues (p. 19).
Step 4 - Respect No-Decompression Dive Limits: The deeper a diver dives and the longer the diver stays underwater, the more nitrogen the body absorbs (p. 19).

quiz_item.question: Why does a scuba diver's body absorb more nitrogen into its tissues during a dive?
options: A. Water pressure increases with depth, forcing nitrogen from breathing air into body tissues
B. Scuba cylinders are filled with 79 percent pure liquid nitrogen instead of normal air
C. Cold water converts carbon dioxide in the bloodstream into nitrogen gas
D. Swimming with fins increases heart rate and blocks the lungs from exhaling
choices: A. Water pressure increases with depth, forcing nitrogen from breathing air into body tissues
B. Scuba cylinders are filled with 79 percent pure liquid nitrogen instead of normal air
C. Cold water converts carbon dioxide in the bloodstream into nitrogen gas

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is the most important rule in scuba diving to breathe continuously and never hold your breath while ascending with compressed air?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is the most important rule in scuba diving to breathe continuously and never hold your breath while ascending with compressed air?
options: A. Holding your breath causes nitrogen gas to freeze inside the first-stage regulator valve.
B. As water pressure decreases during ascent, trapped air in the lungs expands according to Boyle's Law and can rupture lung tissue (pulmonary barotrauma) if not exhaled.
C. Exhaling underwater fogs the inside of your dive mask and drains the buoyancy compensator vest.
D. Breathing continuously allows you to ascend faster than 60 feet per minute without making a safety stop.
choices: A. Holding your breath causes nitrogen gas to freeze inside the first-stage regulator valve.
B. As water pressure decreases during ascent, trapped air in the lungs expands according to Boyle's Law and can rupture lung tissue (pulmonary barotrauma) if not exhaled.
C. Exhaling underwater fogs the inside of your dive mask and drains the buoyancy compensator vest.
D. Breathing continuously allows you to ascend faster than 60 feet per minute without making a safety stop.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. As water pressure decreases during ascent, trapped air in the lungs expands according to Boyle's Law and can rupture lung tissue (pulmonary barotrauma) if not exhaled.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Under Boyle's Law, gas volume increases as surrounding water pressure drops during ascent; holding your breath while breathing compressed air traps expanding gas in the lungs, risking life-threatening pulmonary barotrauma.
